This is the one research group publicly building analysis pipelines exactly over Quebec CITQ and BC provincial STR registration data (gap #12) and Canadian STR commercial-operator/ghost-hostel detection (relevant to gap #9 supply and #2 realized occupancy proxies); their published PDF reports (linked from repos, e.g. via CMHC/McGill) may contain registry-level counts and trends even where the raw data itself is not redistributable, and the strr R package methodology (FREH, ghost-hostel, commercial-operator classification) is reusable on any listing-level panel we already hold (e.g. Inside Airbnb Canadian coverage) as an acquisition/classification method.

This is one of very few active research groups publishing recurring, city-level commercial/multi-listing host concentration numbers -- a proxy for professional-host share of STR supply outside the US, useful context for gap #12 (STR ordinance trackers/registration data) and the multi-listing host theme generally, even without a clean data file to pull.

Confirms UPGo is a real, active (some repos updated 2025-2026) academic STR-research lab exactly matching the theme brief, but their underlying data (AirDNA) is licensed, not open, so the org's value to us is methodology and report structure (ghost-hotel detection, commercial-operator flags, CMHC housing-transition linkage) rather than a data source. Individually flagged repos above are the highest-signal subset; the rest are lower-value variants of the same code pattern.

This is a full academic pipeline for exactly the regulator/compliance lens the persona is tracking: registration-compliance rates, delisting after enforcement, commercial-operator and ghost-hostel classification, and STR<->long-term-rental crossover, across multiple Canadian and one US (LA) jurisdiction, with report-specific data/ folders and reusable R tooling. Feeds gap #12 (registration datasets, regulatory trackers) and gap #13 (STR<->LTR crossover) directly, and the strr package's FREH/ghost-hostel classifiers are a reusable method for identifying quasi-commercial (non-Airbnb-branded) STR supply that competes with or supplies Airbnb's own inventory.

name: RamVasuthevan/city-of-toronto-short-term-rentals-registration
what_it_holds: Git-scraping repo (Simon-Willison-style) that pulls the City of Toronto open-data portal's official 'Short Term Rentals Registrations' CSV (short-term-rental-registrations-data.csv) every day at UTC midnight and commits it. Active as of 13 Sep 2026 (last updated 2026-09-13). Because it commits a fresh CSV daily, the git commit history itself is a genuine point-in-time vintage series of Toronto's STR registration list (registration IDs/status/addresses per the city schema) going back to whenever the repo started running. Has a LICENSE file (type not confirmed) and a short README describing the git-scraping method.
why_useful: Not one of our twelve named US cities, but it is a live, actively-updated, point-in-time (dated-snapshot) municipal STR-registration mirror using the git-scraping pattern gap #17 asks for (Socrata/CKAN discovery + archive tooling); the technique is directly reusable for Austin/Denver/Seattle/etc. Socrata portals.
time_coverage: ongoing daily snapshots, current as of 13 Sep 2026
size_hint: one dated data file per day, size unspecified

Toronto active-registration counts are a legal-supply proxy for a top-10 ABNB market.

A daily, point-in-time count of legally registered Toronto STR units is a regulatory-supply proxy for one of Airbnb's regional mix components (Canada/NA) and directly serves CONTEXT.md gap #12 (city registration datasets) with something better than a one-shot snapshot — the git log gives vintages for free, addressing the point-in-time requirement in CLAUDE.md rule 2.

name: centraldedados/alojamento_local
what_it_holds: Python scraper (fetch_rnal.py, fetch_rnal_setup.py, using Splinter/RoboBrowser) for Portugal's Registo Nacional do Alojamento Local (RNAL), the national short-term-rental licence registry. Covers all 308 Portuguese municipalities; supports selective scraping by municipality range. Includes a municipal reference table (Concelhos_CAOP2018.csv, CAOP 2018 codes). No data is pre-committed to the repo -- running the script produces one CSV per municipality (Down_<DICO>_<NOME>.csv), split into time-period parts for large cities (Lisbon, Porto). 12 commits, 3 stars, 6 watchers; license and last-commit date not visible from the README fetch.
why_useful: Directly targets numbered gap 12 (STR registration/city registration datasets -- explicitly names Lisbon RNAL). RNAL is the closest thing to a full-market STR supply census for Portugal (active listing counts, addresses/parishes, licence dates by municipality), which is not otherwise in our municipal-registry holdings (Austin, Barcelona HUTB, Maui, NYC OSE, California TOT). A working, already-built scraper against a live government portal (not airbnb.com) means point-in-time supply counts for a full EU country could be pulled without violating the airbnb.com scraping restriction -- worth a human call on whether to actually run it.
time_coverage: Current registry snapshot at time of run (not historical/vintage; would need repeated runs for a time series)

name: Inquilinato-Cadiz/mapa
what_it_holds: Astro/Leaflet static site with committed data pulled from OpenRTA, the Andalusian regional tourism registry (Registro de Turismo de Andalucía), CC BY 4.0, refreshed monthly via GitHub Actions. Files: public/data/municipios/<slug>.geojson (per-municipality tourist-dwelling points, filtered to 'vivienda de uso turístico' and 'apartamento turístico' categories, contact info stripped, reprojected EPSG:25830->WGS84), src/data/municipios.json (index), src/data/stats.json (aggregate stats), plus a cadastral large-owner layer (fincas-cadiz.geojson / fincas.json). Covers all 45 municipalities of Cádiz province.
why_useful: A live, automatically-refreshed, geolocated STR-registry dataset for a full Spanish province beyond Barcelona (which we already hold via HUTB) -- fills gap 12 with finer city coverage in Spain and demonstrates OpenRTA as a pullable regional source that could be extended to other Andalusian provinces (Málaga/Costa del Sol, Granada, Seville) for a party of the EMEA STR-supply picture.
time_coverage: Monthly automated snapshots going forward from repo creation; not clear how far back history is retained in git history of the geojson files
size_hint: 45 municipality geojson files + 2 aggregate JSON files, per-listing point data with property type
license: CC BY 4.0 for the underlying OpenRTA data; repo code license not confirmed
